provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The task copies the multicoloured half-shape by a 180-degree point reflection about the interior 8 marker: (y,x) -> (2cy-y, 2cx-x). The original stays in place, and the copy is painted only onto background cells. A point reflection commutes with every D4 transform, so the mapping formula is unchanged in visible coordinates. The only orientation-dependent part is which side of the line holds the shape. In the original it is the left side. A row reversal turns left into right, and each clockwise quarter turn moves left to top, top to right and right to bottom. The factory computes the side as ((2 if d4>=4 else 0) + d4%4) % 4 and emits it as a constant. For the left/right cases the shape is selected by comparing columns to cx; for top/bottom it is selected by comparing rows to cy. The colour roles are specialised as constants: background = palette[7], marker = palette[8], line = palette[4]. The centre is found as the marker cell that touches no grid edge, which stays true under every D4 transform. The edge markers sit at the two ends of the marker row (or column), and in the generator's domain the marker row/column is never on an edge. Rectangular grids work because the line and marker always sit at the middle column and middle row, so no cell is clipped. Bounds checks are kept anyway.
draft_notes.limitations: The palette is assumed to be a bijection, so the shape colours never coincide with the background, line or marker colours. If several interior markers were present (outside the constructor's domain), the first one in row-major order would be used. The archived solver paints colour by colour, but the reflection is injective and only background cells are painted, so the order has no effect on the result. No constructor defects or fixture contradictions were found: all three train pairs and the test pair match the uniform point-reflection rule about the interior marker. The rule text mentions per-colour teaching stages; those are not part of the output and are not reproduced.

independent_source_review.mechanism: Point reflection of the multicoloured half-shape about the interior 8 marker: each shape cell (y,x) is painted at (2cy-y, 2cx-x), but only onto background cells. The original shape is kept. The constructor places the 4 line in the middle column cx=(W-1)//2 and the marker row at cy=(H-1)//2, with 8s at (cy,0), (cy,cx) and (cy,W-1). The emitted solver works directly in visible coordinates. It finds the 8 that touches no grid edge, takes the non-BG/non-LINE/non-MARK cells on a constant SHAPE side, and point-reflects them. A point reflection commutes with every D4 transform, so only the shape side and the palette roles are specialised.
evidence: Labels depend only on the input. The output loop in generate() maps (y,x) to (2*cy-y, 2*c-x) using cy and c, which are visible as the interior marker. The shape's top/height latents only affect the input. OFF_CENTRE_RATE makes 80% of shapes off-centre relative to the marker row, so a bounding-box centre cannot replace the marker.

Reflected cells never clip and never land on non-background cells. Shape rows lie in 1..H-2, so mirrored rows also lie in 1..H-2. Shape columns lie in 1..c-1 (explicit) or 2..c-1 (random, because w<=c-2 gives s=c-depth>=2). Mirrored columns therefore lie in c+1..2c-1=W-2, which excludes the line and the right edge marker. Everything right of the line is background in the input, so the `== BG` guard is always true in the domain.

Sampling is well defined. lo<=hi holds for every h in 4..H-2: cy<=H-2 and h<=H-2 give both bounds. Each row is a contiguous run ending at column c-1. Holes exclude column c-1, and the fringe always keeps the cell next to the line. So the shape stays 4-connected through column c-1, and _connected is also re-checked.

The fallback in _sample_shape keeps margin>=3. Each upper row with a mirror gets (y,c-1) recoloured to differ from its mirror. Rows without a mirror differ trivially, and h>=4 gives at least 3 non-centre rows. This only ensures rotation is distinguishable from a mirror; the label is unaffected.

Shape colours come from {0,1,2,3,5,6,9}, which is disjoint from BG=7, LINE=4 and MARK=8. Under a bijective palette, the solver's exclusions of BG, LINE and MARK are exact. The interior marker is unique, and the edge markers always touch an edge under every D4 transform.

The SIDE constant ((2 if d4>=4 else 0)+d4%4)%4 is the only orientation-dependent constant. A wrong side would reflect nothing (opposite side) or only part of the shape (orthogonal side), so the host's 8000 augmented checks (1000 pairs x 8 D4) passing confirm the convention.

Hand-checked fixtures: train 2 (2,5)->(12,9) gives 1; train 3 (8,2)->(8,14) gives 5. The test hole at (15,7) leaves (3,11) as background in the output, which matches. The archived program also maps the left edge marker (cy,0) onto (cy,W-1), but that cell is non-BG, so this is harmless; the factory excludes MARK explicitly.
There is no whole-grid untransform/solve/retransform wrapper. The solver loops over visible cells with visible-coordinate arithmetic.
The rule involves no arbitrary colour lookup, because colours are copied, so no episode colour-evidence check applies (e729b7be is not in the evidence-check list).
nonblocking_limits: Non-square grids (about 40% of default samples) and sizes outside 15..19 are synthetic extensions. The point-reflection rule extends to them unambiguously because the marker fixes the centre.

The shape side is a D4-specialised constant rather than inferred per grid. This is legitimate orientation specialisation; the solver would not handle a shape placed on the other side, which the constructor never produces.
If several interior markers existed, the solver would use the first in row-major order. The constructor excludes this case.
The solver assumes a bijective palette, so shape colours never alias BG, LINE or MARK.
The per-colour 'teaching stages' in the rule text are not part of the output and are not reproduced.
required_context_checks: Host should confirm the D4 index convention used to compute SIDE matches the augmentation harness for all 8 variants. The supplied audit reports 8000 augmented checks passing, which covers this.
No colour-association evidence check is required for this task.

host_review.resolution: Reviewed constructor invariants, visible-coordinate solver, fixture agreement and documented out-of-domain branches. Source hashes match passing audit.
host_review.augmentation_evidence: All eight D4 transforms are checked in audit; d4=7 is its final loop index. Palette is bijective and shared across all episode pairs.
host_review.limitations: Finite execution/domain evidence, not proof of unrestricted generalization or complete identifiability.
